ADDITIONAL INFORMATION
An interdisciplinary research project

Why do some places renew while others fall behind?

RESPLACES explores how economic structures, human agency and institutions shape regional resilience, path dependence and long-term decline—from old industrial regions to left-behind places.

Explore our research ↗Meet the team →
THE ENGLISHMEN'S FIELD · BILBAO c. 1980 · INDUSTRIAL PORT CONTEMPORARY VIEW · URBAN RENEWAL
THE ENGLISHMEN'S FIELD · THEN & NOW

Drag the arrow left or right to compare Bilbao then and now. The photographs introduce a broader story of resilience in the Basque Country. As Valdaliso, Suárez, Mayor and Magro (2026) show, the Basque regional government, firms, development agencies and technology centres built a coalition that helped modernise existing industries and diversify into new activities—contrasting with the more persistent industrial lock-in in Asturias.

01 / About RESPLACES

Understanding the geography
of economic change.

A historical investigation into how places adapt, remain locked into existing paths, or experience long-term relative decline.

Regions do not simply succeed or fail. Their futures emerge from histories of industrial specialisation, collective decisions and institutional change.

RESPLACES stands for Resilience, Path Dependence and Lock-ins in Old Industrial Regions and Left-Behind Places: Structure, Agency and Institutions in Historical Perspective.

The project brings together economic and business historians, regional scientists and economists to investigate why some former industrial and peripheral regions renewed their economic trajectories after the structural shocks of the late twentieth century, while others struggled to do so.

Building on earlier work in regional resilience, the research connects evidence about firms, industries and institutions with the long-term experiences of territories and communities.

QUESTION 01

Why do regions diverge?

How can places with comparable starting conditions develop along different economic paths?

QUESTION 02

What produces lock-in?

When do stabilising specialisations, institutions and policies become barriers to renewal?

QUESTION 03

Who can change the path?

How do entrepreneurs, governments, organisations and external actors shape local possibilities?

02 / Research areas

Two research axes.
One shared framework.

The project connects the study of old industrial regions with the historical origins and persistence of left-behind places.

Axis 01 / Coordinated by J. M. Valdaliso↗

Industrial resilience
& regional renewal

How do former industrial regions respond to deindustrialisation and structural shocks? We examine regional policy, development agencies, firm and industry resilience, and the agency behind successful—or blocked—economic renewal.

Basque CountryAsturiasCataloniaIndustry & firmsRegional policy
Axis 02 / Coordinated by I. Saitua↘

Left-behind places
& peripheral economies

Why do some rural, mining and peripheral areas experience persistent decline? We investigate historical trajectories, external ownership, resource dependence, institutions and place-based policies through national and international comparison.

Castile and LeónExtremaduraNorth AmericaMiddle East
Across both axes

Structure · Agency · Institutions

A common analytical lens connects the regional, organisational and policy levels across different historical trajectories.

Method 01

Historical measurement

Long-run regional and provincial indicators, employment series and shift-share analysis.

Method 02

Path tracing

Archival research, documentary evidence and analysis of critical junctures, actors and institutions.

Method 03

Comparative analysis

Cross-case comparison and configurational methods (fsQCA) to examine divergent outcomes.
